newsArray.title: ENG v PAK 2026: WATCH - “I'm disappointed,” Joe Root reacts to Brydon Carse being withdrawn from squad after nightclub row
newsArray.description: England Test captain Joe Root has expressed immense frustration, stating he is "really hacked off" and "really disappointed" after fast bowler Brydon Carse was dropped from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan due to a nightclub incident. The disciplinary issue occurred just days after England's dominant victory by an innings and 103 runs over Pakistan in the first Test at Headingley. Social media footage emerged showing Carse in handcuffs being led away by police officers outside a nightclub in Derby at around 4:00 AM on Saturday (August 22). The altercation reportedly began when Carse was refused re-entry into the venue by bouncers. Police briefly arrested him on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly. He was later "de-arrested" and released without charge after agreeing to leave the area. However, the Cricket Regulator has launched an investigation into the matter. As a result, Carse has been officially withdrawn from England’s squad for the second Test at Lord's. Hampshire seamer Sonny Baker has been called up to fill the vacancy in England's squad. "If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off, I'm really disappointed," Root told reporters. "After last week's performance, we're sat here and we're talking about something that is not related to it at all." He also revealed that Brydon Carse had apologised and understood the seriousness of his actions. "I've spoken to Brydon, and when I first found out my main concern was him as a person," Root said. "I don't think I'm speaking out of turn by saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure that when he gets his chance he will say that himself. "But I don't think it's the isolated incident itself, it's the fact we keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field." England captain Joe Root opens up on the nightclub incident involving Brydon Carse ????️ pic.twitter.com/id0H0hIQ5j — Sky Sports Cricket (@SkyCricket) August 25, 2026 Carse was not on active England duty when the nightclub episode took place. He had been released to play for Durham and was celebrating their County Championship victory over Derbyshire alongside teammates Matthew Potts and Ben Stokes. This disciplinary investigation puts renewed spotlight on the England men’s team's off-field culture. Carse is the third England player to be sidelined this summer due to disciplinary issue, following separate incidents involving Stokes, Gus Atkinson, and Harry Brook. Root admitted that the repeated incidents were damaging England's image and that the players had to take responsibility for changing perceptions. "In many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back, and it's something that we're going to have to live and breathe consistently," Root stated. "I might only be in this dressing room for a couple more years, but there is a group of players there who might be in there for another 10." Upon returning to Test captaincy, Joe Root removed the midnight team curfew, placing greater responsibility on the players to make the right choices. "I've made it very clear how we want to conduct ourselves, and now we've got to live it and show people what I see day in, day out in the dressing room, which is a group of characters who know what it means to play for England and not having incidents define how we are seen as players," he said. "That's going to take some work and time." Root clarified he would not be involved in deciding any disciplinary punishment for Carse because the matter was now with the regulator. "I don't think the recent past has been a good look," the skipper said. "It's our responsibility to change that. I see the dressing room every day and how we operate around cricket and it's very impressive. But at the same time, I can understand why we are viewed in a certain way and in a certain light at the moment." Root insisted that the England cricket team must proactively protect its reputation through disciplined off-field behavior. "That's what lies ahead of us, to change that. I just think, if we don't put ourselves in certain situations, it's not something we will have to worry about."

newsArray.title: ક્રિકેટના મેદાન બાદ હવે ગેમિંગની દુનિયામાં રોહિત શર્માની નવી ઇનિંગ, આ કંપનીમાં કર્યું રોકાણ
newsArray.description: ભારતીય ક્રિકેટના સ્ટાર રોહિત શર્માએ હવે ગેમિંગની દુનિયામાં એન્ટ્રી કરી છે. રોહિત શર્મા એક ગેમિંગ કંપનીમાં રોકાણકાર બન્યો છે. ખાસ વાત એ છે કે આ ગેમના લોન્ચ પહેલાં જ લાખો લોકો તેમાં રસ દાખવી ચૂક્યા છે. હવે સપ્ટેમ્બરમાં શરૂ થનારા ટ્રાયલ બાદ તેની લોકપ્રિયતા કેટલી વધે છે તે જોવાનું રહેશે.
creator: smit chauhan
